title: The Kleene-tree node construction swaps the arity and program-index arguments.
details: Van Oosten, Basic Computability Theory, 1993 revised 2013, Theorem 3.2.10 proof, printed p. 32 (PDF page 42). The tree's displayed defining condition uses T(1,i,i,k), testing a unary program of index i on input i. The following paragraph constructing a node of length n instead says to check T(i,1,i,k). Its first two arguments are reversed, so this is not the finite family of constraints defining the tree. Replace that occurrence by T(1,i,i,k). For each i<n, scan k<n for the actual defining constraints; if any has output at most one, set a_i to that output, which is unique by deterministic evaluation. If none does, set a_i=0. This satisfies all the defining constraints and proves the existence of a node of every length. The final separator argument already uses the intended unary predicate T(1,x,x,k). The typo and argument order were visually confirmed in the inspected PDF. This is planning-only source material; no current corpus entry consumes the proof. Current adoption2026-11-09: the separator tree uses correctly ordered diagonal arguments and bit1onA/0onB for the separator ones set, as stated explicitly.
